newsitem.title: CONGO: Kabila rebels massacred Rwandan refugees-witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Kabila rebels massacred Rwandan refugees-witnesses.

text.p: Laurent Kabila's rebels massacred more than 200 unarmed Rwandan Hutu refugees at a port on the Congo River earlier this month and a further 140 at a village to the south, witnesses said.

Priests, civil servants and residents told Reuters the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo (AFDL) killed more than 200 refugees on a quayside at the National Transport Office (ONATRA) port at Mbandaka town on May 13.
They were slaughtered the same day AFDL fighters seized the western town. Dozens more were killed on the main street and on the road to the airport, said the witnesses, who declined to be identified.
New Justice Minister Mwenze Kongolo said in Mbandaka on Thursday that he was sent to investigate reports of killings but none took place and AFDL soldiers had nursed refugees back to health.

The witnesses said the refugees arrived from Wendji village, 20 km (12 miles) to the south, where residents, refugees and Red Cross workers said AFDL fighters had slaughtered about 140 earlier on May 13.
They said some of the Hutu refugees were former Rwandan soldiers and Interahamwe militiamen, but they had already been disarmed by Zairean government troops and there was no fighting.
"I didn't count the number of dead but I am certain that in the town and on the airport road more than 200 were killed. That's what I saw on my way to work that day," said a priest.
Asked how many were systematically massacred on the ONATRA quayside, a senior civil servant said: "Many more than 200."
Witnesses said refugees were forced to kneel or lie down on the concrete quayside and were shot or bayoneted or beaten to death with rifle butts. Most bodies were dumped in the river.
The AFDL has denied exterminating Rwandan refugees in its seven-month thrust across Zaire, renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo when Kabila proclaimed himself president on May 17.
The refugees, who had trekked 1,200 km (750 miles) across the former Zaire in six months, fled Rwanda in 1994 in fear of reprisals for the genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates.

Red Cross officials showed Reuters mass graves at Wendji cemetery, where they said they buried 116 refugees on May 13, followed by 17 on May 14 and seven including a woman and child in following days.
They produced a list detailing the dead including women and children. Pigs came at night to dig at the soil, they added.
They said one small baby boy was still alive when he was taken to the cemetery but was then killed by an AFDL soldier.

"We picked up the kid and brought him to the soldiers and said: 'Look, this one is not dead'. It was a small baby boy. A soldier picked up a chunk of wood and hit it on the head and it died and we buried it. It was sad," said a Red Cross worker.
The aid worker picked up a short, thick piece of wood lying next to the graves and said it was the one the rebel used.

"Alliance troops came and opened fire on the refugees with machineguns. They came with a Landcruiser (vehicle) to the crossroads in town and told us: 'You are safe, it's the refugees that we want'," said an aid worker in Wendji.
"They killed lots of people and even a Zairean watchman was killed. After the massacre, the refugees went into the forest," said a fisherman, who declined to be identified.
Refugees when they arrived in Wendji included former troops and Interahamwe militiamen who led the 1994 genocide of Tutsis and Hutu moderates in Rwanda before fleeing to Zaire.
But they were disarmed in Wendji by Zairean soldiers and the Hutu former soldiers among them fled downstream before May 13 so there was no fighting when the AFDL arrived, witnesses said.

In Mbandaka, residents who went out to greet the AFDL were told to go home. Shortly afterwards, the AFDL soldiers turned on refugees scattered throughout the town and those who had already gathered at the ONATRA port, hoping to head downstream by boat.
Witnesses showed entries in their diaries and drew maps to describe the killings and the precise locations of the bodies.
Scores of green army uniforms, hundreds of army boots, ammunition and hand grenades still littered the floor of a building in Wendji, next to a crossroads, on Friday.
Two refugees, one shivering and apparently near death and the other pointing at worms crawling from a gaping wound on his ankle, still lay in the debris on Friday, begging for help.
A delegation of priests visited new regional governor Gabriel Mala Mutya on Friday because they were outraged he had said in a radio interview no refugees were killed in Mbandaka.

France accused the rebels on May 13 of killing refugees at Mbandaka earlier this month, citing witnesses. The U.N. refugee agency started flying Rwandan refugees from the town back to Rwanda on Thursday.
